verdict.rationale: Google Cloud documents Workload Identity Federation for granting workloads temporary, key-less federated access to resources, and IAM docs describe fine-grained permission scoping — both of which are the building blocks for giving an agent a narrowly-scoped, non-escalating credential. However, none of the evidence ties these mechanisms specifically to AI agents or documents an explicit pattern (e.g., short-lived token issuance, escalation-prevention guardrails) for agentic workloads. Missing for 10: agent-specific credential-scoping guides, explicit anti-escalation controls, and hands-on validation that WIF/IAM patterns are used this way in practice for AI agents.
